newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index breaks support level.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index breaks support level.

text.p: Philippine shares pierced through a major support in late Wednesday trade as investors dumped stocks in favor of higher yield fixed-income instruments, traders said.
The main index broke its 2,600 support-level, tumbling 61.24 points to 2,594.62.

"This high interest rate is sapping liquidity out of the stock market to fixed-income securities. Hence, the selldown," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
Despite assurances from bank officials that interest rates will not stay high for long, the central bank kept its overnight rates at a 2-1/2 year high for a week now to protect the peso.

"There's the negative sentiment generated by higher interest rates. The trend should be reversed if they come down. Until then foreign investors are not keen on jumping into the market and locals would play with fixed-income instruments," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities.
Among the active losers in late trade are index heavyweights Petron Corp, Meralco B, Metrobank and PLDT.
